react_result.final_narrative_text: A metabolomics experiment comparing control and treatment groups revealed a coordinated elevation of five eicosanoid and oxylipin metabolites that collectively point to intense activation of the arachidonic acid cascade. Cross-paradigm enrichment — RaMP multi-DB ORA (WP:WP167 Eicosanoid synthesis, FDR 6.97×10⁻¹⁴), Mummichog m/z-direct activity (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p=0.00109), and MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG:hsa00590, p=0.0169) — converged on the same biological theme, providing strong consensus despite FELLA being unavailable. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the central driver; its lipoxygenation products leukotriene A4 (C00909) and 5(S)-HETE (C04805) via 5-LOX, and its CYP450/LOX oxidation products 15(S)-HETE (C04742) and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) via 15-LOX and non-enzymatic dehydration, respectively, are all elevated in the treatment arm. The leukotriene branch (LTA4 → inflammation) and the cyclopentenone branch (15d-PGJ2 → PPARγ activation) suggest a dual proresolution and inflammatory response. Phenytoin (C07443, an anticonvulsant drug) and 3-methyladenine (C00913, a purine analog) are outlier metabolites not enriched in any top-ranked pathway, consistent with an off-target or exogenous origin. The three-pathway consensus with four shared driver metabolites establishes arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological story.
